proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\). By definition, \(\delta(P)\geq\delta_0>0\), and fixed relevance within \(\mathcal P_W\) gives \(\|\beta(P)\|_2\geq c_\beta>0\). The endpoint-domain lemma and the parameter margin give
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)] \tag{1}
\]
without \(K\)-truncation.

On the open neighborhood of \(\Sigma(P)\) on which \(\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{zz})>m_\Sigma/2\), \(\|\beta\|_2>c_\beta/2\), and \(\delta>\delta_0/2\), the maps
\[
 \Sigma\longmapsto\alpha=\Sigma_{zz}^{-1}\Sigma_{zy},\qquad
 \Sigma\longmapsto\beta=\Sigma_{zz}^{-1}\Sigma_{zx},\qquad
 (\alpha,\beta)\longmapsto\check\theta
 =\frac{\beta'\alpha}{\|\beta\|_2^2} \tag{2}
\]
are continuously differentiable. So are
\[
 \lambda=\|\alpha-\check\theta\beta\|_2^2,
 \qquad \delta=\tau^2-\lambda,
 \qquad \theta_\pm=\check\theta\pm\frac{\sqrt\delta}{\|\beta\|_2}, \tag{3}
\]
because all divisions and the square root in (2)--(3) occur on domains bounded away from zero. This proves the claimed differentiability.

The eighth-moment restriction supplies the moments required for the multivariate central limit theorem applied to
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \operatorname{vech}\{W_iW_i'-\Sigma(P)\}. \tag{4}
\]
Moreover, centered independent sampling gives \(\sqrt n\,\overline W_n\overline W_n'=o_P(1)\). Taylor expansion of (2)--(3) around \(\Sigma(P)\), combined with (4), yields
\[
 \sqrt n\left\{
 (\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})
 -(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P))\right\}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,V_P), \tag{5}
\]
where \(V_P\) is obtained by applying the derivative in (2)--(3) to the covariance influence vector; the Gaussian law may be degenerate. Since \(\widehat\delta_n\to_P\delta(P)\geq\delta_0\), the positive-part convention is inactive with probability tending to one. The ridge-totalization lemma makes the resolvent correction \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) on an event whose probability tends to one. Hence (5) applies to the totalized endpoints.

Finally, the fixed-interior specialization of the adaptive score-hull theorem gives
\[
 E_Pd_{\to}\{C_n,\Theta_I(P)\}=O(n^{-1/2}). \tag{6}
\]
Thus the contact-robust procedure retains the ordinary root-\(n\) endpoint limit and root-\(n\) outer set loss at every fixed interior law.

We give a finite-dimensional proof tailored to the quadratic score. Let \(m=(d+2)(d+3)/2\), let \(\operatorname{vech}\) be a fixed isometry from symmetric \((d+2)\)-by-\((d+2)\) matrices into \(\mathbb R^m\), and define
\[
 V_{i,P}=\operatorname{vech}\{W_iW_i'-\Sigma(P)\},
 \qquad S_{n,P}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nV_{i,P}. \tag{1}
\]
Centered independent sampling gives \(E_PV_{i,P}=0\), and the eighth-moment restriction gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_P\|V_{i,P}\|_2^4<\infty. \tag{2}
\]
Covariance conditioning makes every \(\Sigma_{zz}(P)\) invertible with inverse norm at most \(m_\Sigma^{-1}\). On the neighborhood where the instrument block has smallest eigenvalue at least \(m_\Sigma/2\), explicit differentiation of the inverse shows that the first two derivatives of \(S\mapsto\mathfrak q_n(S;\theta)\) are bounded uniformly in \(\theta\in K\), \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), and all sufficiently large \(n\). In particular,
\[
 \psi_P(W_i;\theta)=a_P(\theta)'V_{i,P},
 \qquad
 a_P(\theta)=a_{0,P}+a_{1,P}\theta+a_{2,P}\theta^2, \tag{3}
\]
where the three coefficient vectors are uniformly bounded. This follows from
\[
 D\{A^{-1}b\}[H]=A^{-1}(h-H_AA^{-1}b),
 \qquad D\|u\|_2^2[du]=2u'du. \tag{4}
\]

The centered covariance obeys
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma(P)
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{W_iW_i'-\Sigma(P)\}
 -\overline W_n\overline W_n'. \tag{5}
\]
Fourth-moment expansion using (2) gives
\[
 \sup_PE_P\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma(P)\|_{\mathrm F}^4=O(n^{-2}),
 \qquad
 \sup_PE_P\|\overline W_n\|_2^8=O(n^{-4}). \tag{6}
\]
Let \(\mathcal E_{n,P}=\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Sigma_{zz,n})\geq m_\Sigma/2\}\). The eigenvalue variational inequality and Markov's inequality applied to (6), equivalently the established ridge-totalization lemma, imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}P(\mathcal E_{n,P}^c)=O(n^{-2}). \tag{7}
\]
Taylor's formula, (5)--(6), and the \(n^{-2}\) ridge resolvent bound give on \(\mathcal E_{n,P}\)
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}\left|
 \sqrt n\{\widehat q_n(\theta)-q_P(\theta)\}
 -a_P(\theta)'S_{n,P}\right|=\rho_{n,P},
 \qquad
 \sup_PE_P[\rho_{n,P}\mathbf1_{\mathcal E_{n,P}}]=O(n^{-1/2}). \tag{8}
\]

The sample counterpart of (3) is also a polynomial of degree at most two in \(\theta\). With \(\Omega_P=E_P[V_{i,P}V_{i,P}']\), expansion of its finitely many coefficients and (2) gives
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in K}\left|
 \widehat\sigma_n^2(\theta)-a_P(\theta)'\Omega_Pa_P(\theta)
 \right|=o_P(1) \tag{9}
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_W\); on \(\mathcal E_{n,P}\), this difference is bounded in \(L^2\) by \(Cn^{-1/2}\). Score nondegeneracy therefore implies
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_W}P\left\{
 \inf_{\theta\in K}\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\geq c_\sigma/2
 \right\}\longrightarrow1. \tag{10}
\]
Thus denominator truncation is asymptotically inactive.

Conditionally on the sample, the multiplier process is a centered Gaussian polynomial of degree at most two. After studentization it has the representation
\[
 \frac{\widehat{\mathbb G}_n^\xi(\theta)}
      {\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\vee n^{-1}}
 =u_n(\theta)'G_n, \tag{11}
\]
where \(G_n\) is standard Gaussian in dimension at most three and \(\|u_n(\theta)\|_2\leq1\). Consequently,
\[
 \widehat c_{1-\eta}^+
 \leq Q_{1-\eta}\{\|N(0,I_3)\|_2\}=:c_\eta<\infty. \tag{12}
\]

We prove uniform conditional approximation by contradiction. If it failed, some sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_W\) would have failure probability bounded away from zero. The matrices \(\Omega_{P_n}\), the three bounded coefficient vectors in (3), and the finitely many coefficients of \(\sigma_{P_n}^2(\theta)\) lie in compact Euclidean sets, so pass to a convergent subsequence. For each fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^m\), (2) permits the uniform characteristic-function expansion
\[
 E_{P_n}\exp\{it'V_{i,P_n}/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t'\Omega_{P_n}t}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}). \tag{13}
\]
Raising (13) to the \(n\)-th power proves that \(S_{n,P_n}\) converges to a centered Gaussian vector with the limiting covariance. Every entry of the empirical covariance driving (11) is an average of a polynomial of degree at most four in \(W_i\), whose variance is bounded by the eighth-moment restriction. Hence that empirical covariance converges in probability to the same limiting covariance, and (5)--(6) make the sample polynomial coefficients converge to their population counterparts.

The map from these finitely many coefficients to the supremum over compact \(K\) is continuous under uniform coefficient convergence, because \(c_\sigma>0\) prevents division by zero. Along the selected subsequence,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{P_n}(T_{n,P_n}),
 \mathcal L_\xi(T_n^\xi\mid W_1,\ldots,W_n)
 \right)\longrightarrow0 \tag{14}
\]
in \(P_n\)-probability, contradicting the assumed failure. Thus (14) holds uniformly over \(\mathcal P_W\).

For quantile transfer, each subsequential Gaussian limit has the form
\[
 H(G)=\sup_{\theta\in K}v(\theta)'G,
 \qquad \|v(\theta)\|_2=1, \tag{15}
\]
on its effective Gaussian support. Its \((1-\eta)\)-quantile is at least \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\eta)>0\), because the supremum dominates any fixed \(v(\theta_0)'G\). Write \(G=RU\), with the Gaussian radius \(R\) independent of its direction \(U\). Conditional on a direction with \(H(U)>0\), \(RH(U)\) has a continuous radial density; directions with \(H(U)\leq0\) cannot create an atom at a positive value. Hence (15) has no atom at its positive \((1-\eta)\)-quantile. Compactness of the coefficient limits turns this subsequential fact into uniform upper-quantile continuity. Combining it with (14) yields
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_W}
 P\{T_{n,P}\leq\widehat c_{1-\eta}\}\geq1-\eta. \tag{16}
\]
Replacing the supremum over \(K\) in (16) by the smaller set \(\Theta_I(P)\) proves assertion (A) of the theorem.

On \(\mathcal E_{n,P}\), define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{n,P}={}&n^{-1/2}
 +\sup_{\theta\in K}|\widehat q_n(\theta)-q_P(\theta)|\\
 &+n^{-1/2}\widehat c_{1-\eta}^+
 \sup_{\theta\in K}\{\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\vee n^{-1}\};
 \end{aligned} \tag{17}
\]
on \(\mathcal E_{n,P}^c\), set \(R_{n,P}=n^{-1/2}\). Equations (2), (6), (8)--(9), and (12) give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}E_PR_{n,P}=O(n^{-1/2}). \tag{18}
\]
The same calculations with squares give \(\sup_{n,P}E_P[(\sqrt nR_{n,P})^2]<\infty\), which proves uniform integrability of \(\{\sqrt nR_{n,P}\}\). If \(\theta\in C_n\), its defining inequality implies
\[
 \widehat q_n(\theta)
 \leq n^{-1/2}\widehat c_{1-\eta}^+
 \{\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\vee n^{-1}\}. \tag{19}
\]
Adding the uniform score error in (17) gives \(q_P(\theta)\leq R_{n,P}\) on \(\mathcal E_{n,P}\), and the first term in (17) gives \(R_{n,P}\geq n^{-1/2}\). This proves assertions (B)--(C). Every bound is uniform over the uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\), and therefore over its contact and fixed-interior subclasses.

(2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) establish, for the scalar \(L_2\) leakage model with \(p=2\) and an unrestricted scalar effect domain, that the raw sharp set is empty when \(\delta(P)<0\) and is the interval \([\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\) when \(\delta(P)\geq0\). This note separately restricts the effect parameter to \(K\), so its target is \(\Theta_I(P)=\{\theta\in K:q_P(\theta)\leq0\}\): it is empty when \(\delta(P)<0\), and it equals \(K\cap[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\) when \(\delta(P)\geq0\). The unrestricted raw interval is the published input; intersection with \(K\) is this note's parameter-space restriction.

proposed.statement: For each fixed \(P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\), the raw endpoints are well defined, the maintained parameter margin gives \(\Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\) without \(K\)-truncation, and the endpoint map is continuously differentiable at \(\Sigma(P)\). Hence \(\sqrt n\{(\widehat\theta_-^{\mathrm{tot}},\widehat\theta_+^{\mathrm{tot}})-(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P))\}\) has the ordinary delta-method Gaussian limit, and the same multiplier hull \(C_n\) has root-\(n\) outer loss. This is the regular special-case reduction of Watson et al.'s smooth endpoint argument.
proposed.justification: The reduction verifies that contact-robust inversion sacrifices neither the smooth endpoint limit nor root-\(n\) loss away from tangency.
proposed.gap: Watson et al.'s smooth argument applies after a fixed positive slack is imposed; this proposition states that domain and connects it to the proved hull.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\eta<1/2\), \(\bar H>0\), \(\bar T>0\), and the contact and fixed-interior Gaussian-witness compatibility regimes. There are constants \(c_{\mathrm{ct}}>0\) and \(c_{\mathrm{int}}>0\), depending only on \(\eta,\bar H,\bar T,a_{\mathrm{int}}\) and the fixed class constants, with the following properties. For every \((D_n)\in\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{ct}}\), there exists \(N_{\mathrm{ct}}(D)<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N_{\mathrm{ct}}(D)\) with \(\sqrt n\geq2\bar H\),
\[
 \sup_{h\in[0,\bar H]}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[d_{\to}\{D_n,\Theta_I(P_{n,h})\}\right]
 \geq c_{\mathrm{ct}}n^{-1/4}. \tag{1}
\]
For every \((D_n)\in\mathfrak D_{\eta}^{\mathrm{int}}(a_{\mathrm{int}},\bar T)\), there exists \(N_{\mathrm{int}}(D)<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N_{\mathrm{int}}(D)\) satisfying \(\bar T/\sqrt n\leq\min\{a_{\mathrm{int}}/2,(1-a_{\mathrm{int}})/2\}\) and \(2a_{\mathrm{int}}\bar T/\sqrt n+\bar T^2/n\leq1-a_{\mathrm{int}}^2-\delta_0\),
\[
 \sup_{t\in[-\bar T,\bar T]}E_{P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}}\!\left[d_{\to}\{D_n,\Theta_I(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}})\}\right]
 \geq c_{\mathrm{int}}n^{-1/2}. \tag{2}
\]
The interior witness-membership theorem gives \(P_{n,t}^{\mathrm{int}}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\) throughout this quantified regime. Together with the multiplier-hull upper theorem, these inequalities give matched \(n^{-1/4}\) contact and \(n^{-1/2}\) interior frontiers under the same outer directed-loss convention.
proposed.justification: The converse shows that fourth-root contact loss is information-theoretic and matches the now-proved upper hull.
proposed.gap: The result strengthens generic nonregularity into explicit leaky-instrument directed-Hausdorff lower bounds in both local experiments.
proposed.consumer: The two lower bounds provide certified benchmarks for alternative endpoint and score procedures.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The final sentence is synchronized with the proved, rather than conditional, multiplier-hull upper theorem.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(C_n=\{\theta\in K:\sqrt n\,\widehat q_n(\theta)/(\widehat\sigma_n(\theta)\vee n^{-1})\leq\widehat c_{1-\eta}\}\), with uniform whole-identified-set coverage over the uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_W}\{\sqrt{\delta(P)}+n^{-1/4}\}E_P[d_{\to}\{C_n,\Theta_I(P)\}]=O(n^{-1/2})\); in particular, contact loss is \(n^{-1/4}\) and fixed-interior loss is \(n^{-1/2}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The functional summary must record the discharged coupling theorem, its exact upper-bound class, and the stronger continuous elbow rather than a conditional two-regime claim.

prose_updates.tldr: Taking Watson et al.'s unrestricted raw \(p=2\) interval as a published input, this note intersects it with \(K\) and studies tangent contact. The total positive-part plug-in endpoints have a fourth-root Gaussian law, while the fully specified feasibility-retained bootstrap converges to a random truncated kernel and is not contact-uniform. The uniform multiplier-coupling theorem, discharged at main commit c1414705685e, makes inversion before the square-root map uniformly cover the whole identified set on the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). Its exact continuous elbow yields \(n^{-1/4}\) contact loss and \(n^{-1/2}\) fixed-interior loss under the same rule. The Gaussian bootstrap counterexample and the minimax converse use laws inside the published model and therefore transfer upward to Watson et al.'s broader \(p=2\) class; the upper hull guarantee is not claimed for that unrestricted class.

project_justification.fill: The project keeps the causal target distinct from its observed-law score representation, takes Watson et al.'s unrestricted raw interval as a published input, and imposes the intersection with \(K\) itself. It derives the fourth-root contact law and the retained random kernel for an exact Efron algorithm, proves nonuniformity for that named workflow, and constructs an every-sample multiplier score hull using a common ridge convention. The uniform multiplier theorem discharged at main commit c1414705685e gives whole-set coverage throughout the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\), while the exact score-set modulus gives a continuous loss elbow and matched contact and interior Gaussian LAN frontiers. The bootstrap counterexample and converse transfer to the broader published \(p=2\) model, but the upper guarantee does not.

prose_updates.related_work: Watson et al. (2024, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7) supply the unrestricted raw \(p=2\) sharp interval; intersection with \(K\) is imposed by this note. Their Theorem 4 supplies the feasibility-retained endpoint-bootstrap workflow. The exact finite-\(B_n\) Efron algorithm, its negligible zero-retention fallback, the contact endpoint law, retained random kernel, nonuniformity result, score hull, continuous loss elbow, and matched frontiers are not attributed to that paper. Andrews (2000) supplies local boundary-sequence logic, and Fang and Santos (2019) distinguish a regular Gaussian primitive from a nonsmooth transform. Romano and Shaikh (2010) inform the whole-identified-set coverage criterion; Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos (2023) inform constrained-score inversion; and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) inform multiplier and anti-concentration arguments. The finite-dimensional quadratic-score proof adapted here fully discharged the paper's multiplier question at main commit c1414705685e, but only on the strict uniformly regular subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). Hirano and Porter (2012) rule out regular estimation of nondifferentiable functionals; the present Gaussian LAN calculations sharpen that diagnosis to matched fourth-root and root-\(n\) directed-Hausdorff frontiers. The bootstrap counterexample and converse witnesses belong to Watson et al.'s broader published \(p=2\) model, whereas the upper hull guarantee does not extend beyond \(\mathcal P_W\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform upper theorem is deliberately limited to the strict subclass \(\mathcal P_W\): fixed dimension, known leakage radius, uniform covariance conditioning, a bounded eighth moment, score-variance bounds, parameter-space margin, and fixed relevance are load-bearing. It does not establish a multiplier approximation for Watson et al.'s unrestricted \(p=2\) class, weak instruments, growing dimension, unknown leakage radius, or contact with the boundary of \(K\). The expected-loss elbow also uses the theorem's integrable root-\(n\) score-band radius; distributional coupling alone would give coverage but not the displayed risk bound. The Gaussian bootstrap nonuniformity witness and the minimax converses require none of that upward extension of the upper theorem and remain valid in the broader published class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7 supply the unrestricted raw \(p=2\) interval. This note separately restricts the target to \(K\), so the identified set is the \(K\)-restricted score sublevel set and the raw square-root endpoints are used only at nonnegative slack. The parameter margin removes \(K\)-truncation on the maintained contact-local and fixed-interior regimes. The uniform multiplier-coupling theorem was fully discharged at main commit c1414705685e and proves whole-set coverage plus the continuous expected-loss elbow on the strict uniformly regular fixed-relevance subclass \(\mathcal P_W\). That upper theorem uses fixed \(d\), known scalar leakage radius, uniformly conditioned covariance, bounded eighth moments, nondegenerate score variance, compact parameter margin, and relevance bounded away from zero; it is not asserted for Watson et al.'s unrestricted class. By contrast, the explicit Gaussian bootstrap counterexample and both minimax lower-bound paths lie within the published model, so those negative and converse conclusions transfer upward. All finite-sample covariance operations use the stated ridge convention, and the directed loss is defined when a random hull is empty.
